page: Amazon Web Services m8i.4xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose server type hosted on the AWS Nitro System. Compute capacity is delivered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running up to 3.9 GHz, configured with 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs. The hardware platform includes an extensive 480 MB L3 cache and supports specialized vector and matrix instruction extensions including AVX-512, Intel AMX (amx_tile, amx_int8), and SHA-NI. The instance is equipped with 64 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 7 GHz, providing a standardized 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per vCPU.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded and text-handling throughput. Geekbench single-core execution ranks in the upper 25%, with text processing evaluating in the top 10% tier. Compression workloads also post competitive results, with single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression both placing in the top quartile. Multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng execution, Clang compilation, PassMark scores, and Redis throughput, consistently sit in the middle 50% band. Lightweight machine learning inference with small 135M parameter models achieves top 25% text generation rates, though larger models align with median performance.

The m8i.4xlarge configuration features an 8 Gbps baseline network interface but does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators like GPUs. As persistent data requires network-attached EBS storage volumes, high-throughput local scratch disk tasks represent an architectural tradeoff. From a resource-density perspective, the combination of DDR5 memory and updated Intel Xeon microarchitecture offers predictable, balanced compute power. The instance is targeted at web applications, CI/CD software build pipelines, microservices, and mid-tier transactional databases that depend on network-attached persistence.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i.4xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. The server delivers 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores at 3.9 GHz, coupled with 64 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a 4 GB per vCPU allocation. It features an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero bundled local storage, and comprehensive instruction set support including Intel AMX and AVX-512. Benchmarks reveal strong single-thread execution, placing in the top 25% for single-core Geekbench tests and compression operations, while text processing ranks in the top 10%. Multi-core compute, static web serving, and database throughput align with median cloud standards. Without integrated local storage or GPU acceleration, the m8i.4xlarge provides a balanced, reliable environment tailored for web applications, enterprise software stacks, containerized services, and CI/CD build environments utilizing network-attached block storage.
